html:
On 26 May 1908 a British drilling team struck oil at Masjed Soleyman in southwest Persia. It was the first big oil find in the Middle East.

The search was paid for by William Knox D'Arcy, who had bought a concession from the Qajar shah in 1901, and it had nearly run out of money. In 1909 the Anglo-Persian Oil Company was set up to work the field, with a pipeline to a refinery at Abadan on the Gulf.

Britain's navy was then switching from coal to oil, and in 1914 Winston Churchill had the government buy a controlling share in the company. Persian oil became a pillar of British power, and Iranians resented how little of the money they saw. In 1951 Mohammad Mosaddegh nationalised the industry, and a British and American backed coup removed him in 1953. The company became BP.
